title: The Northern Journeys

named.name: Tyre
named.label: left
named.note: The great Phoenician port. "The district of Tyre and Sidon" was Gentile territory; there a Canaanite woman asks for "the crumbs" and is praised for her faith (15:21–28).

named.name: Sidon
named.label: left
named.note: Mark 7:31 says Jesus went back "through Sidon" to the Sea of Galilee and the Decapolis.

named.name: Magadan
named.label: left
named.note: Probably Magdala, home of Mary Magdalene ("Dalmanutha" in Mark 8:10). A first-century synagogue was excavated here in 2009, with the carved "Magdala stone" showing the Temple menorah.

named.name: Caesarea Philippi
named.label: right
named.site: Banias, at the foot of Mount Hermon
named.note: At one of the springs of the Jordan, by a cave sacred to the god Pan; Herod the Great built a temple to Augustus here, and his son Philip refounded the town. Here Peter confesses, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (16:16).

named.name: Mount Hermon
named.label: right
named.note: Matthew does not name the mountain of the Transfiguration. Hermon (2,814 m), above Caesarea Philippi "after six days," fits "a high mountain"; Mount Tabor has been the traditional site since the fourth century. Some suggest Mount Meron.

named.name: Capernaum
named.label: right
named.note: Back in Capernaum, the collectors of the Temple tax come to Peter, and the coin is found in the fish's mouth (17:24–27).

named.name: Decapolis
named.label: right
named.site: the Ten Cities, mostly east of the lake
named.note: A league of Greek cities (Hippos, Gadara, Scythopolis and others). Mark 7:31 places the return from Tyre "in the region of the Decapolis."

moves.text: Jesus withdraws to the district of Tyre and Sidon
Back by way of Sidon and the Decapolis (Mark 7:31) to a mountain by the Sea of Galilee
By boat to the region of Magadan
Leaving the Pharisees, they cross to the other side
North to the region of Caesarea Philippi
"After six days": up a high mountain with Peter, James and John
Through Galilee and back to Capernaum

symbols.key: Seven loaves and a few fish: the 4,000 fed
symbols.label: 4,000 fed

symbols.key: Peter's confession: "the keys of the kingdom of heaven"
Transfigured: "His face shone like the sun"

p: These chapters take Jesus beyond Jewish Galilee: to the Phoenician coast, the Greek cities of the Decapolis, and the pagan shrine-town of Caesarea Philippi. The second feeding, of the 4,000 with seven loaves, probably took place on the eastern, Gentile shore, a sign alongside the first among the villages of Israel.
The cave at Banias was thought to lead down to the underworld. Against that backdrop Jesus says, "on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it" (16:18).
